proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the matched log-free n^(-r/(2r+3)) regret rate for r in [1,3], a same-original-record converse, constant-order unknown-r adaptation, and capped closure graphs of size O(n log^2(en)) and O(n log^3(en)). D0.5 passed the mathematics and all four cited-source checks, but rated the completed public randomized Gaussian benchmark subfield with score ceiling 6.7, below the required field floor. Independent terminal validation confirmed no bounded repair within the original scope; the run was banked downgraded with re-raise status, and no Lean formalization was entered.
tldr: The original-record minimax causal welfare regret over all interacting coordinatewise nondecreasing two-score dose policies is \(n^{-r/(2r+3)}\), uniformly for \(r\in[1,3]\), with no necessary logarithm or iterated logarithm. The exact uniform covariate and scalar-dose design, bounded dose-Hölder mean, unit-variance Gaussian response, and supplied common independent Gaussian-noise potential-outcome completion define a controlled benchmark with proved causal identification. The explicit common-policy graded learner attains the rate, and a legal original-Gaussian packing gives the matched converse. Its capped dyadic spatial schedule and sufficient dose-label grid give \(O(n\log^2(en))\) vertices and edges per known-index closure graph. All approximation and numerical errors are budgeted, and the output is exactly monotone on the continuum. The unknown-index holdout learner has optimal constant-order simultaneous adaptation and \(O(n\log^3(en))\) aggregate training-graph size. Total real arithmetic is polynomial. The result is a prospective precision benchmark for an interacting extension of Ai--Fang--Xie's additive monotone duration policies; their JTPA data are not asserted to follow this benchmark.
gap: Critical monotone complexity bounds leave a logarithmic gap, while continuous-dose kernel policy theory does not determine which logarithms are genuine welfare loss on the unrestricted interacting class.
fill: A new dose-scale and spatial-resolution coupling must turn threshold-ring bounds into sharp regret for one computable policy, with a converse calculated from the original scalar-dose likelihood.
